title: Optional Transformers.js local backend behind a flag
description: Add an optional sentiment backend using Transformers.js with a small local ONNX model (e.g. distilbert-sst2 or Cardiff Twitter RoBERTa), downloaded once and cached locally, selectable behind a flag. It must never be loaded by default and must not break the no-network-imports privacy guard for the default path. Compare against VADER on the gold set and on a real-corpus agreement check where only aggregate agreement numbers are recorded. Measure throughput of both backends on this M1. Done when: both backends run locally, throughput and agreement numbers are recorded, and the default stays VADER unless evidence says otherwise.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Optional transformer backend added: @huggingface/transformers (optionalDependency) with Xenova/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english q8, cached under ~/.cache/dataparade/sentiment-models after the one-time download (66 MB); loaded only via --sentiment-backend transformer so the default path never touches it. Backend selection reworked into async factories (createSentimentBackendAsync) with pre-scored dedupKey maps feeding the sync computeMeter. Committed scripts/sentiment-backend-eval.ts (runs under ts-node because onnxruntime-node cannot execute tensors inside jest's vm realm). Results on BlackbookM1: gold accuracy transformer 22/34 (0.647) vs vader 34/34 (1.000) - the binary SST-2 head labels 11/14 neutral messages negative and has no neutral concept; real-corpus label agreement vs vader 33.7% overall (3009 messages, window all, aggregate numbers only); throughput vader ~23123 msgs/sec vs transformer ~494 msgs/sec.
